title: OKR Loom: Initiative Stitching & Decision Flow for Quarterly Roadmaps
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: As the company scales, multiple teams propose initiatives that appear to map to the same company objective but have different success metrics, timelines, and dependencies. This creates duplicate effort, unclear ownership, and fragile cross-team rollouts.

Objective: Create a repeatable, lightweight process and artifact (the 'OKR Loom') that stitches initiatives to company-level OKRs, surfaces decision owners, and enforces a minimal evidence bar for commitment in the quarterly roadmap. The Loom should enable PMs and Eng leads to: 1) see overlap/conflict across initiatives, 2) surface required dependencies across teams (infra, runtime, compliance), and 3) have a documented decision flow for conflicting prioritization.

Scope: Company-level OKRs only (not feature-level backlog grooming). Deliverables: Loom template (Confluence), acceptance criteria checklist, a lightweight decision-playbook, training doc for squad leads, and a one-off synthesis workshop agenda for this quarter. Excludes detailed resourcing or sprint plans (teams remain responsible for execution).
acceptance_criteria: Confluence OKR Loom template published with fields for hypothesis, expected key results, success metrics, timelines, dependencies, risk register, and decision owner.
Synthesis process defined: weekly triage cadence for cross-team conflicts, owner escalation ladder, and a single Slack channel with bot reminders.
Two pilot initiatives (Console UX performance and Dedicated autoscaling) stitched into the Loom with resolved dependency maps and documented decisions.
One training session run with all PMs + Eng leads and positive feedback from at least 8 participants.
Rollout checklist created and used by three teams to gate roadmap inclusion for Q2.
Clear rubric for 'evidence bar' defined (perf telemetry, customer requests, cost delta estimate, security signoff when required).

Should finance provide an early-stage cost estimate template or is a rough back-of-envelope acceptable for Loom gating?
